title: Anna, eighty-four (Luke 2:36–40)
hookLine: a widow who never left the temple speaks of the child to all who waited

cards: Some congregations have a woman like this. She's been there longer than anyone. She knows where the spare candles are kept.

She was praying in that pew before the current pastor was born. She's buried a husband, maybe more than one friend, and she keeps coming, early, every time the doors open. Visitors walk right past her.
And she's often the one who notices when something real is happening. Right after Simeon, in the same temple, Luke introduces her ancient counterpart, in three short verses.

teach.h: OF THE TRIBE OF ASER, OR ASHER.
teach.b: In the King James Bible: "And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser." Aser is Asher, one of the tribes of Israel.

teach.h: ANNA IS THE GREEK FOR HANNAH.
teach.b: And Anna is the Greek form of Hannah, the name of the Hannah whose song echoed in Mary's.
She was married only seven years, and then: "she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day."
Even in English the line reads two ways: she was eighty-four, or she'd been a widow eighty-four years, which would make her far older. Translations differ.

Either way: years of the same faithful routine, in the same place, waiting. Then: "she coming in that instant gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem."
After all those years, her timing is perfect.
Simeon sings and blesses. Anna talks, to everyone who's been waiting like her. In a way she's one of the first people in Luke to tell others about Jesus.
Some readers notice Luke pairing a man and a woman: Zechariah and Mary, Simeon and Anna.

teach.h: SHE DEPARTED NOT FROM THE TEMPLE.
teach.b: Then the family goes home to Nazareth, and the child grows strong, filled with wisdom, the grace of God upon him.
A week crowded with waiting people: Mary's yes, Mary's song, Zechariah's Benedictus, the census, the shepherds, Simeon. And Anna, who never stopped.

how: Anna is remembered with Simeon at the feast of the Presentation on February 2 in some churches, and Orthodox and Catholic Christians honor her as a saint.

o: the wife of Simeon, who waited with him in the temple
a widowed prophetess who prayed in the temple for years
a priest's daughter who sang a psalm at John's naming

games.q: what's inside Luke 2:36–40 — tap the pairs.
p: spoke of him to all who waited

s: Luke clearly says Anna was eighty-four years old
the line can mean she was eighty-four, or that she had been a widow for eighty-four years.
Anna was married only seven years
Luke says she lived with a husband seven years, and then was widowed.
Anna was from the tribe of Judah
she was from the tribe of Aser, or Asher.

games.q: you're Anna. you've prayed in the temple night and day for years, and you've just seen the child Simeon is holding. what do you do?
o: go quietly back to your prayers.
give thanks, and tell everyone who's been waiting.
ask the parents to stay in Jerusalem.
games.why: she gives thanks and "spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem." Simeon sings; Anna tells.

practice: Bring to mind an older woman whose faithfulness shaped you or someone near you: a grandmother who prayed for you, a neighbor who always asked how you were, the woman at church who remembered your name; she doesn't have to share your beliefs, just to have kept showing up.
Picture her face and the place you'd usually find her, and let yourself be grateful for the years she gave. If you pray, give thanks for her by name; if not, hold her in gratitude.

wordCard.voice: Anna. A prophetess, widowed young, who prayed in the temple night and day for years, and told everyone who was waiting about the child.

orig.note: Hebrew: Hannah, the name of Samuel's mother. Anna is its Greek form.

carryVoice: Your line: she never stopped. Years of showing up, and then that instant. Another week on the path.
